questions.q: What kind of reaction takes place at the cathode of a galvanic cell?
questions.explain: Reduction takes place at the cathode and oxidation at the anode. In a galvanic cell the cathode is positive.

questions.q: What will happen if an external potential of 1.30 V is applied to a Daniell cell (E° = 1.10 V)?
options: The cell will give current as before
The reaction will occur in the opposite direction (it will become an electrolytic cell)
questions.explain: If E external > E°cell, the flow of electrons is reversed and the cell becomes electrolytic: Cu dissolves and Zn is deposited.

questions.q: E°(Zn²⁺|Zn) = −0.76 V and E°(Cu²⁺|Cu) = +0.34 V. What is E°_{cell} of the cell Zn | Zn²⁺ || Cu²⁺ | Cu?
Which of the following metals cannot liberate H₂ from dilute HCl?
questions.explain: The E° of Cu is positive (higher than the 0.00 V of H⁺|H₂); so it cannot reduce H⁺.

questions.q: What is the emf of the cell Zn | Zn²⁺(0.01 M) || Cu²⁺(1 M) | Cu at 298 K? (E° = 1.10 V)
Which is correct when a galvanic cell reaches equilibrium?
questions.explain: At equilibrium the emf of the cell is zero and the reaction quotient Q equals the equilibrium constant K.

questions.q: What is Δ_{r}G° if E° = 0.50 V and n = 2? (F = 96500 C mol⁻¹)
What happens to κ and Λ_{m} when an electrolyte solution is diluted?
questions.explain: κ decreases because the number of ions per unit volume decreases. But in Λ_{m} the volume also increases and the attraction between ions falls, so Λ_{m} increases.

questions.q: What is Λ°_{m} of Na₂SO₄? (λ°(Na⁺) = 50.1, λ°(SO₄²⁻) = 160.0 S cm² mol⁻¹)
questions.explain: Kohlrausch law: Λ°m = 2 × 50.1 + 160.0 = 260.2 S cm² mol^{−1}.

questions.q: How many faradays of electricity are needed to reduce 1 mol of Al³⁺ to Al?
questions.explain: Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al; 3 mol of electrons for 1 mol of Al, i.e. 3 F.

questions.q: How much Ag will be deposited at the cathode of an AgNO₃ solution by a charge of 965 C? (Ag = 108, F = 96500 C mol⁻¹)
What is produced at the cathode when an aqueous solution of NaCl is electrolysed with Pt electrodes?
questions.explain: Reduction of water (E° = −0.83 V) is easier than reduction of Na⁺ (E° = −2.71 V). So H₂ is released at the cathode and NaOH is left in the solution.

questions.q: Which of the following is a secondary battery?
questions.explain: A lead storage battery can be recharged by passing current in the opposite direction.

questions.q: Why does iron coated with zinc not rust even when a scratch exposes the iron?
options: Because the E° of Zn is more positive than that of Fe
Zn (E° = −0.76 V) is more reactive than Fe (−0.44 V); Zn becomes the anode and corrodes, and Fe becomes the cathode and stays protected
Because the paint deposited on Zn covers the iron
questions.explain: This is called sacrificial protection: the more reactive metal (Zn) is itself oxidised and protects the iron.
